title: The Best Programs to Earn Star Alliance Gold Status
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Star Alliance Gold status comes with access to all Star Alliance lounges. Photo: Star Alliance.
Star Alliance Gold status is handy to have when flying with any of the 26 alliance members. These include Singapore Airlines, Air New Zealand, ANA, Thai Airways and Air Canada. Here’s a full overview:
Star Alliance airlines.
Once you’ve earned Star Alliance Silver or Gold status, you’ll enjoy reciprocal elite benefits (such as lounge access and priority at the airport) whenever you fly with any other Star Alliance airline. A full list of Star Alliance status benefits is available on the Star Alliance website .
With most Star Alliance frequent flyer programs, you earn status based on the number of miles you’ve flown (taking into account a multiplier for the fare class) on Star Alliance airlines throughout the year. You’ll earn miles at a different rate depending on the airline you’re flying and the fare class you book .
But some airlines make it a lot easier than others to achieve status with their loyalty program! So, which is the best frequent flyer program for earning Star Alliance status?
This guide analyses 9 Star Alliance frequent flyer programs that are likely to be of most interest to Australians. It explains how to earn the equivalent of Star Alliance Silver and Gold status with each program. The guide concludes with an analysis of the best overall Star Alliance frequent flyer programs.
Singapore Airlines KrisFlyer
A Singapore Airlines A380 at Sydney Airport. Photo: Jonathan Wong.
Singapore KrisFlyer is a popular choice for Australian travellers for several reasons. Firstly, KrisFlyer status is recognised when flying with Virgin Australia. Secondly, there are many opportunities to earn KrisFlyer miles in Australia through credit cards and KrisFlyer miles are a valuable currency.
However, earning KrisFlyer status is more difficult than earning status with some other Star Alliance programs. Here are the requirements to earn and maintain KrisFlyer status:
KrisFlyer Elite Silver (Star Alliance Silver) – earn 25,000 Elite miles within 12 consecutive months
KrisFlyer Elite Gold (Star Alliance Gold) – earn 50,000 Elite miles within 12 consecutive months
Status is valid for 12 months from the earn date. See the Singapore Airlines website for more details.
You can earn KrisFlyer Elite miles on all Star Alliance airlines and flights on low-cost subsidiary Scoot. You can also earn Elite miles on codeshare flights operated by Virgin Australia. But the big catch for Australians is that you can’t earn Elite miles for Virgin Australia marketed flights – only codeshares with an “SQ” flight number.
United MileagePlus
A United Airlines Boeing 787 at Brisbane Airport. Photo: Matt Graham.
United MileagePlus could be a good program if you’re just starting out with Star Alliance and fly to the USA a lot, because it offers a status match. With the United status match challenge , you can get four months of free United MilagePlus Premier status. To extend this, you’d need to fly a minimum amount on United Airlines during the trial period.
Another benefit of United MileagePlus is that it’s one of the only Star Alliance frequent flyer programs to award miles on the cheapest Economy fare classes when flying with Air New Zealand and Lufthansa Group airlines (including Lufthansa, Swiss, Austrian and Brussels Airlines).
United also partners with Virgin Australia , which is a “preferred partner” of United. MileagePlus Gold, Platinum and 1K members can access benefits including lounge access when flying on Virgin Australia. You can even earn Premier Qualifying Credits for Virgin Australia flights.
Unfortunately, earning or retaining United MileagePlus status requires quite a lot of flying – especially if you don’t live in the United States. You now need to earn Premier Qualifying Points (PQP) and/or Premier Qualifying Flights (PQF) to earn or maintain United status.
1 PQP is equivalent to 1 US Dollar spent on United flights, excluding taxes. For flights marketed by partner airlines, the earn rate is based on the distance flown and a multiplier based on the fare class purchased. Meanwhile, 1 PQF is equivalent to 1 flight.
There is an additional requirement to take at least four flights operated by United Airlines or United Express each year . To do this without visiting the USA, you can fly on a fifth-freedom route operated by United such as Tokyo-Ulaanbaatar or Hong Kong-Bangkok.
United Airlines MileagePlus status requirements
Here are the requirements for earning and maintaining United Airlines status in 2026:
Premier Silver (Star Alliance Silver) – 15 PQF + 5,000 PQP or 6,000 PQP only within a calendar year
Premier Gold (Star Alliance Gold) – 30 PQF + 10,000 PQP or 12,000 PQP only within a calendar year
Note that United updates its status requirements yearly, so the goalposts might change in future years.
After earning United status, it’s valid until the end of January in the year after next (i.e. the rest of the calendar year, plus 13 months). See the United website for more details.
United status would best suit somebody flying regularly to or within the United States. Unfortunately, if you have United status, you don’t automatically get access to United Club lounges when flying within the USA (even if you have a First Class ticket). But you are eligible for complimentary upgrades, Economy Plus seating and other extra benefits only on United aircraft.
The United Club in Denver (B Gates East). Photo: United Airlines.
United is also one of several Star Alliance airlines to offer lifetime status through its Million Miler program . You can receive lifetime Gold status after earning 1 million miles, with more benefits after reaching 2, 3 and 4 million lifetime miles.
Aegean Miles+Bonus
An Aegean Airlines A320neo. Photo: Aegean Airlines.
Earning Star Alliance Gold status via the Aegean Miles+Bonus program is relatively easy, compared to other programs, especially if you visit Greece at least once per year!
Unfortunately, Aegean made changes in 2026 that make it harder to earn status. But the new rules could still work for some people.
If you take at least 12 Aegean or Olympic flights each year, Aegean reduces the number of tier miles needed to qualify for Star Alliance Gold status. And once you already have Gold status, the renewal requirement is reduced again! (Previously, you just had to take 4 Aegean or Olympic flights annually to access this benefit.)
Aegean and Olympic Air are based in Athens. If you’re in Europe, you can relatively easy fly four Aegean/Olympic sectors by flying from somewhere in Europe to a Greek Island via Athens, and back. Do this three times to get to 12 sectors.
Here are the requirements for earning Aegean Miles+Bonus status from 2026:
Silver (Star Alliance Silver): Earn 12,000 tier miles within 12 months (including at least 4 Aegean/Olympic flights) or 36,000 tier miles otherwise
Gold (Star Alliance Gold): Earn 24,000 tier miles within 12 months (including at least 12 Aegean/Olympic flights) or 72,000 tier miles otherwise
Here are the requirements to renew Aegean Miles+Bonus status:
Silver (Star Alliance Silver): Earn 9,000 tier miles within 12 months (including at least 4 Aegean/Olympic flights) or 36,000 tier miles otherwise
Gold (Star Alliance Gold): Earn 18,000 tier miles within 12 months (including at least 12 Aegean/Olympic flights) or 72,000 tier miles otherwise
See the Aegean website for details.
You can also purchase tier miles from Aegean for €50 per 500 tier miles. There is an annual purchase limit of 1,000 tier miles for Blue members, 2,000 tier miles for Silver members or 3,000 tier miles for Gold members. Theoretically, this means you could requalify for Gold status by earning as few as 9,000 tier miles per year from flights in a normal year.
